features.title: Notion OAuth login redirect
features.user_visible_behavior: Clicking 'Continue with Notion' sends the user to Notion's authorize screen.
verification: Start the server: cd server && npm start.
Assert HTTP 302 and the redirect URL points to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with the configured client_id and redirect_uri.
evidence: server/api/auth.ts router.get('/') builds the authorize URL and calls res.redirect.
Covered by the ./init.sh baseline smoke check.

features.title: OAuth callback upserts the user and redirects to /Dashboard
features.user_visible_behavior: After authorizing on Notion, the user is returned, their profile is stored, and they land on /Dashboard.
verification: Complete the Notion OAuth flow against http://localhost:3001/auth/callback with a valid code.
Verify a User row is upserted in Postgres (email, name, notionId, workspaceId, avatar).
Verify the browser is redirected to http://localhost:3000/Dashboard exactly once (no double-send).
evidence: Fixed double-send in server/api/auth.ts success branch: now `return res.redirect('http://localhost:3000/Dashboard')` only (removed the trailing res.json).
Error paths verified 2026-07-01: GET /auth/callback (no code) -> HTTP 400; GET /auth/callback?code=bogus -> HTTP 400 (Notion rejects), 0 occurrences of ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT in server log.
Baseline smoke check still passes after the change.
Manual OAuth run verified 2026-07-01: real Notion login redirects once to /Dashboard (404 there is expected until dash-001) and the User row was upserted correctly in Postgres.
features.notes: Passing. Success path confirmed by a manual Notion OAuth run (single 302 to /Dashboard + User upsert). The /Dashboard 404 is tracked separately by dash-001. (.env key is CLIENT_SECERT and the code matches it - left as-is on purpose.)

features.title: /Dashboard route renders after login
features.user_visible_behavior: An authenticated user sees the dashboard shell at /Dashboard instead of a 404.
verification: Start the frontend: npm run dev.
Assert HTTP 200 and the dashboard shell renders.
evidence: Added app/Dashboard/page.tsx: a server component (no data fetching) rendering the dashboard shell (header + placeholder region). Root app/layout.tsx wraps it.
Redirect target confirmed from source: server/api/auth.ts:81 returns res.redirect('http://localhost:3000/Dashboard') (capital-D), matching the app/Dashboard/ folder.
Verified 2026-07-01: ./init.sh baseline smoke check still PASSES (/auth/ -> 302, / -> 200).

Verified 2026-07-01: npm run dev, then curl http://localhost:3000/Dashboard -> HTTP 200 (was 404); response body contains the shell copy 'Edit conflicts detected across your Notion workspace.' Dev server torn down (port 3000 -> 000), clean state.
features.notes: Passing. Shell only (200 render) — listing conflicts is tracked by conflict-002, which will extend app/Dashboard/page.tsx once conflict-001 lands. No auth gate added on purpose (the verification curls /Dashboard with no session and expects 200).

features.title: Fetch and snapshot Notion pages/blocks per workspace
features.user_visible_behavior: After connecting, the user's Notion pages and block snapshots are stored for the workspace.
verification: Trigger a sync for a connected workspace.
Verify Page rows exist for the workspace (notionPageId, tittle, workspaceId).
Verify Snapshot rows are created linking blockId, pageId, and userId.
features.notes: Prisma models Page and Snapshot already exist in prisma/schema.prisma.

features.title: Detect concurrent edits and record Conflict rows
features.user_visible_behavior: When two users edit the same block around the same time, a conflict is recorded.
verification: Create two snapshots for the same blockId by two different users.
Verify a Conflict row is created with pageId, blockId, user1Id, user2Id, and status='open'.
features.notes: Prisma model Conflict already exists (relations ConflictUser1/ConflictUser2).

features.title: Dashboard lists conflicts with status and resolver
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard shows detected conflicts with their status and who resolved them.
verification: Seed at least one Conflict row.
Verify the conflict appears in the list with its status and resolvedBy value.
